That living an aimless life if fine. Do what makes you happy no matter what. If traveling makes you happy, just start. You'll figure it out as you go. Living in a big house makes you happy, work your ass off and make money. Just do what you want, you're going to be completely gone and forgotten one day. Enjoy it in any way you want.

Figure out what you want out of life. Doesn't have to be super detailed, in fact, the fewer details the better. Just figure out what you want to do with your life for the next five years.

It helps if you keep a journal. Write it down. Write down what you want out of the next five years. What kind of job do you want to have? How much weight do you want to lose? Little things like that. Get it down on paper, so you can look it over and figure put your options, how you can achieve those desires.

Be realistic. Don't shoot for the moon because you haven't even figured out how to fly yet. A big problem is easiest to solve when you break it down into problems you can tackle in your own time at your own pace.

To take your idea further, it helps to break goals down into Daily / Weekly / Monthly / Yearly / 5-Year / Lifetime perspectives, ideally taking your ideas from high-level (lifetime), and making those aims more concrete the closer you funnel down to your daily activities. It's also important to hold yourself accountable by regularly writing about your goals (like you suggested) and reflecting on why you did or didn't meet them. If you failed to meet any of your goals, it's worth exploring why you failed to reach that goal, and to reevaluate whether it's really something that's important to you, and whether you need to reassess your approach to accomplishing it.
